PullRequest.Title: sessions: Track editor chat cohorts in Agents telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Track editor-window chat usage so Agents window telemetry can distinguish user cohorts based on prior editor activity.

- Persist session starts by bounded provider category, total accepted messages, same-window and all-editor-window overlap counts, and last-message time in machine-local shared application storage.
- Include cohort fields in `agents/firstTimeWindowOpen` and `agents/requestSent`, reporting seconds since the last editor message rather than an absolute timestamp.
- Count queued and steering submissions once, excluding retries, queue drains, system/hidden messages, and Agents window activity.

## Implementation notes
- Counters use ordinary shared-storage reads/writes with separate keys per counter/provider. They are intentionally best effort: overlapping window writes can undercount. No new atomic storage API is introduced.
- Cross-window overlap uses a 200ms live probe; unresponsive windows may be missed. The all-window count includes overlap known to the submitting window.
- Telemetry contains bounded provider categories, counts, and elapsed seconds, not session resources or message content.

## Validation
- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed
- Staged-file hygiene — passed
- Focused chat submission, cohort tracking, telemetry, and window-handoff suites — 136 passing
- Client type check, ESLint, and layer checks — passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The 200 ms timeout, pending-set lifecycle, and blocking shutdown join are explicit and deterministic. Only how often users close within that interval is uncertain, which is reflected in low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Shutdown join time waiting on 200 ms timer-backed probe promises
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Any submission during the 200 ms before close/reload adds a pending operation; because probes run concurrently, delay is bounded by the latest probe's remaining timeout but can approach the full 200 ms after the most recent submission.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked window close or reload for up to 200 ms
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this contribution, closing or reloading an editor window had no editor-usage probe promise to join and therefore no telemetry-imposed 200 ms wait.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every accepted request creates a probe that resolves only after a peer response or the 200 ms timeout. The added shutdown listener joins `Promise.all(pending)`, and desktop lifecycle explicitly awaits default joiners before the window closes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 114 newly joins all pending cross-window telemetry operations during shutdown; those operations are introduced at lines 92-105 and use a 200 ms timeout.
Findings.Title: Do not hold shutdown open for the telemetry probe timeout
Findings.Impact: In the common single-window/no-responding-peer case, closing or reloading shortly after sending a chat message visibly waits for the remainder of the 200 ms telemetry timeout, even though this accounting is documented as best effort.
Findings.Evidence: The promise is added to `pending` after scheduling `disposableTimeout(..., 200)` and has no earlier completion when no peer replies. `NativeLifecycleService.handleWillShutdown` awaits `Promises.settled(joiners)`, and the lifecycle contract states joined promises block application closing. Line 114 places all such timer-backed operations into that blocking phase.
Findings.Recommendation: On shutdown, synchronously dispose/finalize outstanding probes and record the local counters without waiting for remote replies, or split baseline recording from the optional cross-window increment so the best-effort remote check never joins the shutdown critical path.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed synchronous listener, broadcast fan-out, lazy model getter side effect, full-list getter, and extension-host refresh RPC are all directly traced in repository code. The exact session/window counts vary, affecting magnitude but not the mechanism or reachability.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension-host IPC refreshes, synchronous cached-session parsing, and per-window session-array allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For one accepted message, work grows across all W open editor windows; a previously idle peer can refresh each of its P registered providers, and every probe scans/materializes its C chat models plus S persisted agent sessions, yielding O(W*P) provider refreshes and O(W*(C+S)) local work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive cross-window IPC/CPU and increased latency returning from an editor chat send
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, accepting an editor chat message did not broadcast a probe, access `IAgentSessionsService.model`, parse the agent-session cache, or refresh session providers in unrelated windows; the delayed service/model stayed lazy until a feature that displayed or used agent sessions requested it.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new `hasOtherSession` closure reads `agentSessionsService.model.sessions`. It is called synchronously for the submitting request and by every window receiving the new broadcast probe. The first read creates `AgentSessionsModel`, parses all cached sessions, and calls `resolve(undefined)`; that path refreshes every registered controller, with extension controllers crossing `$refreshChatSessionItems` IPC. Subsequent probes still materialize and deduplicate the entire historical session array.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 52 newly dereferences `agentSessionsService.model.sessions` from the telemetry predicate; added line 80 invokes that predicate for every incoming cross-window probe, and added line 91 invokes it synchronously for every accepted local submission.
Findings.Title: Keep telemetry probes from activating every window's session providers
Findings.Impact: Sending one editor chat message with several VS Code windows open can activate and refresh all chat-session providers in every idle peer window, while the submitting window synchronously pays full-history setup/scanning before `sendRequest` returns. Users with multiple windows or large agent-session histories can see first-send latency and a burst of extension-host/provider work unrelated to the requested chat.
Findings.Evidence: `Emitter.fire` delivers the new acceptance listener synchronously. This closure dereferences the lazy `agentSessionsService.model`; its getter constructs `AgentSessionsModel`, whose constructor parses `agentSessions.model.cache` and whose service getter invokes `model.resolve(undefined)`. `resolve` schedules every registered provider, `refreshChatSessionItems` calls each controller's `refresh`, and extension-backed controllers implement that as `_proxy.$refreshChatSessionItems`. The `sessions` getter also converts the complete map to an array and runs full-list deduplication before `some`. The broadcast receive path calls the same closure in every peer.
Findings.Recommendation: Answer telemetry from a lightweight set/count of currently in-progress resource IDs that is maintained by existing status/model events, and let probe handling inspect only already-initialized state. In particular, do not dereference the lazy agent-sessions model or call its full `sessions` getter from this best-effort telemetry path; if no lightweight state exists yet, expose a non-activating peek rather than resolving providers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send or queue a user chat request from an editor window while other editor windows are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `ChatService.sendRequestInternal` starts the request/queues it, then synchronously fires `onDidAcceptRequest`; before `sendRequest` returns, the new listener scans local chat/session state and posts the cross-window probe. Peer responses, provider refreshes, the 200 ms wait, and storage accounting are off the request-response critical path, although lazy model construction/cache parsing in the synchronous listener is on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast one probe and receive up to one response from each live editor peer through `BroadcastChannel` (or synchronous localStorage fallback).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outbound probe per accepted submission, delivered to W-1 editor windows; each busy peer may send one response. There is no coalescing across submissions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cross-window probe or response was sent for chat submissions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Posting occurs before the acceptance listener returns; peer handling and responses are asynchronous and off the submitting request's immediate critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate and refresh chat-session item controllers; extension-backed controllers call `$refreshChatSessionItems` in the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On first model access in each previously idle window, up to P registered providers are refreshed concurrently; one submission can trigger this independently in W windows, for O(W*P) refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The delayed agent-sessions model and its providers remained inactive until agent-session UI/functionality explicitly requested them; a chat submission in another window did not activate them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous model/cache construction is on the submitter listener path. Provider refreshes are delayed per provider and asynchronous, so they create background IPC/load rather than blocking the response directly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist bounded usage counters to application-shared storage, whose renderer cache flushes through storage IPC/database updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two to five counter keys plus last-message date per accepted submission, coalesced by the storage layer's 100 ms flush into generally one update batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor submissions did not write these shared usage counters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the probe response/200 ms timeout and is off the send critical path; shutdown may flush pending storage through the existing storage close joiner.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number W of open editor windows, P registered session providers per window, C live chat models, and S persisted agent sessions. Effective work is O(W*(C+S)) state inspection per probe and can add O(W*P) first-touch provider refreshes; storage writes remain bounded per submission.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Broadcast delivery fans out to all peer windows concurrently. Within each newly initialized model, provider resolves use `Promise.all` and per-provider delayers, but there is no cross-window limiter, so aggregate provider refresh concurrency grows with W*P. Storage coalesces same-window key updates over 100 ms.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The agent-session model initialization and workspace cache parse happen once per window, but every later probe still materializes/deduplicates the full session collection. Probe results are not cached or coalesced. Shared-storage reads are from the initialized in-memory cache; writes are delayed/coalesced by storage.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: synchronous event delivery, lazy model side effects, full-array getters, broadcast fan-out, provider Promise.all, and extension-host RPC are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical users may have only one window and modest history, but multi-window users with several providers or long session histories receive the full fan-out. Exact extension/provider refresh duration is implementation-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary-fanout regression: best-effort telemetry now activates/scans unrelated windows and provider inventories.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close, quit, or reload an editor window shortly after sending a chat request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Desktop lifecycle fires `onWillShutdown` and awaits all default joiners before closing. The new joiner waits for all outstanding probes, each of which otherwise settles only on a peer response or its 200 ms timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential application-shared storage update/flush after the probe settles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced counter batch for submissions that settle while storage remains writable; the storage flush is existing infrastructure, while these keys are new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No editor-usage counter update was pending at shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The deterministic regression is waiting for the timer-backed telemetry promise; any resulting storage flush can also join the existing shutdown path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Submissions made in the final 200 ms before shutdown. Multiple probes settle concurrently, so delay is bounded by the most recent probe's remaining timeout and can approach 200 ms.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All pending operations are awaited with `Promise.all`; concurrency prevents additive N*200 ms waits but does not remove the latest timer deadline.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or negative response shortens the common no-peer case; absence of a peer is learned only by the fixed timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: timeout creation and native lifecycle join semantics are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Closing/reloading within 200 ms of submission is intermittent, but when triggered the blocking interval is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity shutdown latency regression; best-effort telemetry should not block close/reload.

Scenarios.Scenario: Emit Agents-window request and first-open telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On each Agents request, `getTelemetry` synchronously reads bounded counters before the existing asynchronous workspace-file-count path emits telemetry. First-open telemetry reads the same counters at timer/shutdown emission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read up to 17 bounded shared-storage values and JSON-serialize at most 12 provider counters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per Agents request and once for the first-open event; provider cardinality is statically bounded to 12.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These bounded counter reads and the small provider-map serialization were absent from these telemetry events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads hit the storage service's initialized in-memory cache; no new filesystem/IPC read is performed. Serialization is constant-bounded and precedes existing telemetry emission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit existing `agents/requestSent` or `agents/firstTimeWindowOpen` telemetry with five additional bounded fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional event; one richer payload per existing event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events were emitted without the five editor-usage fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The PR does not add an extra telemetry call. Request telemetry remains behind the existing workspace-file-count promise; first-open uses the existing emission path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Agents request count; each event adds constant bounded reads and payload size independent of chat history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed concurrency; the request event retains its existing async workspace-count sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage values are warm in-memory after storage-service initialization. There is no unbounded telemetry cache or payload growth because providers are enumerated from a fixed list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the bounded in-memory behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible bounded CPU/serialization cost; no evidence of user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: richer telemetry adds constant-bounded cache reads and no new event/boundary call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore an ordinary editor window without using chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At `WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore`, the new contribution checks the window kind, captures delayed service proxies, creates one `BroadcastChannel`, and registers listeners. It does not access `agentSessionsService.model` until a submission or incoming probe.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create one browser `BroadcastChannel` and event listener per editor window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one channel per editor window for the contribution lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No editor-usage broadcast channel was created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Construction runs during BlockRestore, but performs no filesystem/network/provider work in the normal BroadcastChannel path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant allocation/listener per editor window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No work is scheduled until a message is accepted or a peer probe arrives.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Injected delayed services remain proxies at startup; the agent-session model is still lazy until the closure is invoked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser fallback environments may touch localStorage when posting later, not during startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup finding: the eager startup allocation is small and constant; the reportable eager/provider work occurs on the first submission/probe scenario instead.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files and all diff pages. Reported the cross-window lazy-service/provider fan-out and the timer-backed shutdown join. Bounded telemetry reads/payload growth and the single startup channel do not meet the regression threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
